images.title: A pile of answers
images.purpose: Show that a pile of paper slips with answers is hard to read, and ask how to show what the class likes.
images.composition: One loose pile of slips on the left with wide space, and one large question mark on the right.
images.exact_structure: Left: a pile of exactly 6 equal white paper slips, slightly overlapping, each slip showing one simple flat fruit drawing: 2 apples (teal outline), 2 bananas (amber), 2 mangoes (reddish purple #CC79A7). Right: one large grey #6B7280 question mark. No numbers, no table, no graph. Exactly 1 pile and 1 question mark.
labels: How can we show it clearly?
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any number, count, table, tally or graph anywhere in the frame
any people, faces or classroom scene
images.takeaway: A pile of answers needs to be shown clearly.
images.description: A pile of 6 paper slips with fruit drawings on the left and a large question mark on the right, asking how to show the class answers clearly.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the pile and say why it is hard to see what the class likes.

image_decisions.why: The opening idea is a pile of answers and an open question; one simple picture carries it.
